one_liner: Experimental Java 26 HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 server on raw io_uring; out-runs nginx's custom C module on HttpArena's plaintext profiles.
what_it_does: A Linux-only Java HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 server (optional TLS through the system OpenSSL 3, opportunistic kTLS) that lets handlers be written as plain blocking methods annotated with @Get/@Post, @QueryParam and a RequestBody parameter. It is a framework with its own builder API (CardiganServer.builder().port().eventLoops().routes(...)), not a drop-in for nginx configuration; it serves application routes you write in Java, with no proxying, static-site or config-file model of its own.
how_it_is_fast: Thread-per-core, shared-nothing event loops, each pinned to a CPU and driving its own io_uring ring through Panama FFI with SINGLE_ISSUER, DEFER_TASKRUN, registered files, provided-buffer rings and multishot accept/receive (no epoll fallback). Handlers run as virtual threads whose scheduler is the ring-owning carrier itself (via the internal Loom builder), so a blocking read parks on the same core that owns the socket; responses are encoded straight into native egress buffers and pipelined HTTP/1 replies are batched. The HTTP/1 parser is a Java port of picohttpparser and JSON uses a Vector API port of simdjson.
when_to_use: Experimenting with a JVM service where small, CPU-cheap HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2 handlers dominate and you want io_uring-class throughput without async/reactive code.

Plaintext HTTP/1.1 with many keep-alive connections or heavy pipelining on a dedicated Linux 6.1+ x86-64 box (HttpArena baseline-4096 3.95M req/s, pipelined-4096 45.7M req/s on a 64-core Threadripper).
HTTP/2 cleartext or TLS fan-in where nginx's HTTP/2 stack is the bottleneck (14.5M req/s at baseline-h2-256 vs nginx 3.4M), and a JDK 26 preview runtime is acceptable.
Research or benchmarking of Loom-plus-io_uring designs; the code is MPL-2.0 and the repo documents its scheduler in detail.
when_not_to_use: Production: 0.1.0-alpha.5, 28 commits, one maintainer, 1 star, public API and configuration declared experimental, and it depends on --add-opens java.base/java.lang (APOLOGY.md) with no compatibility promise across JDK releases.
Anything outside 64-bit Linux 6.1+ with full io_uring support: it refuses to start rather than fall back when a required ring feature is rejected, and containers need seccomp relaxed for io_uring.
As an nginx replacement for reverse proxying, static files with caching rules or config-driven sites: it is an application framework, not a web server product.

Short-lived-connection or tail-latency-sensitive loads: at limited-conn-4096 it is level with or behind nginx, h2o, mongoose and the C io_uring engines, and its p99 on json-tls-4096 is 205.72 ms vs nginx 52.31 ms.
Memory-tight deployments: the HttpArena container ran a 512 MiB-2 GiB heap and showed 1.2 GiB RSS at baseline-4096 (up to 5.9 GiB at baseline-h2c-4096), vs 75-105 MiB for h2o and libreactorng.

integration.form: Maven artifact dev.cardigan:cardigan (0.1.0-alpha.5), a JAR library you embed
integration.dependencies: No runtime Maven dependencies (JUnit is test scope); system libssl.so.3/libcrypto.so.3 via Panama when TLS is enabled; JVM flags --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED, --add-opens java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED, --add-modules jdk.incubator.vector (HttpArena also passes --enable-preview)
integration.min_toolchain: JDK 26 with the incubating Vector API, Maven 3.9+
integration.platforms: 64-bit Linux 6.1+ only (x86-64 is the regularly exercised target); kTLS optional, TLS 1.3 kTLS needs OpenSSL 3.5+ and kernel rekey support
integration.thread_safety: Each event loop owns its connections and native resources on one pinned carrier; ordinary handlers run as virtual threads on that carrier and may block; @Isolated moves CPU-heavy or untrusted blocking work to a separate carrier pool; @DecodedBody decoders must be bounded, non-blocking and thread-safe.

gotchas: Harness parity (derived from page data): HttpArena's bandwidth/rps gives about 66 bytes per baseline response for cardigan (status line, Content-Type, Content-Length, body) against about 142 for nginx, 114 for libreactorng and 103 for h2o; cardigan sends no Date header (RFC 9110 requires one from an origin server with a clock) and no Server or Connection header, while nginx's module response carries all three, so cardigan writes roughly half the bytes per request. HttpArena's validate.sh checks only Content-Type, so this is legal for the suite but not equal work.

On the h2/h2c rows the top servers converge at 14.5-16.1M req/s while using only 13-30 of the 64 server hardware threads (cardigan 1474% CPU at baseline-h2-256, agensio 1953%, h2o 3033%), which suggests h2load rather than the server sets the ceiling; the 4.2x and 6.2x over nginx measure nginx (6485% CPU, server-bound), not a lead over other fast HTTP/2 stacks.
Virtual-thread scheduling uses an internal JDK builder through --add-opens java.base/java.lang; a JDK update can break it, and the same opening is used to read compact String bytes on hot paths.

HttpArena runs pull the 0.1.0-alpha.5 Maven artifact, not the repo HEAD, and the benchmark entry was written and submitted by the cardigan author; the cardigan repo itself publishes no benchmark numbers and points to HttpArena.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over Vert.x, Quarkus, Helidon SE or Netty when you want blocking-style Java handlers with io_uring thread-per-core throughput and can live with an alpha on JDK 26 preview; the C# minima-sync, zeemo, zix, vanilla and libxev rows beat it at baseline-4096 (4.31-4.44M vs 3.95M req/s), so on raw HTTP/1 throughput it is not the leader even among non-C entries.
verified_claims_summary: On HttpArena's 64-core AMD Threadripper PRO 3995WX (loopback, server and load generator on separate CPU halves, 5 s runs, best of 3), cardigan 0.1.0-alpha.5 on Temurin JDK 26 served 3,947,346 req/s at baseline-4096 vs 3,284,513 for nginx 1.31.4 with a custom C module built -O3 -march=native (1.20x, derived from page data), and 14.5M/15.1M req/s on baseline-h2-256/h2c-256 vs nginx 3.4M/2.5M. C io_uring engines libreactorng (4,377,377) and libioma (4,255,834) beat it on the same board, and cardigan's rows were saved days after nginx's in separate runs.
status_note: Active alpha (last commit 2026-09-02, releases alpha1 to alpha5 between 2026-08-08 and 2026-09-02, no issues filed), MPL-2.0 with MIT/Apache-2.0 ported files; usable for experiments, not for production until it stops depending on JDK internals and preview features.
